post.description:
Record what the caller's device can do about push (SVC-255). Logs only.

SVC-255 is about providers who never receive notifications, and nobody can
currently say how many that is. Sentry captures registration *failures*, but
with no denominator — and no existing request carries the platform, so there
is nothing to mine retroactively. The version check looks like it would help
and does not: it reads a static `latest.json` and picks the platform branch
on the client, so the server never sees which one.

Deliberately stores nothing. One structured line, counted in CloudWatch
Insights. The question is "should we invest in the iOS path at all", which
needs answering once — a column on `users` would answer a different
question ("which providers should we chase") and is only worth adding if
the distribution says the problem is real.

Fire-and-forget from the client's side: a failure here must never affect
whether push itself registers.

get.description:
Open job offers for the current provider (SVC-254).

The fallback delivery path. Until this existed, an FCM push was the only way
an offer reached anyone — so a stale token, a denied notification permission
or an iOS Safari tab meant the provider was silently deaf to paid work.

The provider app polls this while online. Each entry is the same
``BookingOfferResponse`` the push route's card fetches, so a polled offer and
a pushed one are indistinguishable to the UI. Soonest-expiring first.

Also tops up: a provider who came online after a booking was dispatched has
no offer row for it, and its push has already been sent. This is the only
place they can be added, so the read writes the missing rows.

get.description:
What the provider's next transfer will actually be (SVC-303).

Distinct from `/me/earnings/summary`, which answers "what have I earned".
This answers "what is coming to me", and the two differ by real money:

* **cash commission** — on a cash job the provider collected the full amount
  at the door, so the platform's 20% is netted off their next online
  transfer;
* **the T+1 settlement gate** — a completed job is only payable once
  Razorpay has deposited that money with us, since paying from platform
  float is not permitted.

So `pending_amount` is the wallet-derived figure the payout will really
send, `gross_amount` is what the queued jobs are worth before netting, and
the frontend shows the difference rather than letting the provider discover
it at the bank.

Names no future payout date: payouts are admin-triggered and there is no
schedule, so any date here would be invented.

The provider's own payout statement, newest first (SVC-303).

Reads `settlement_statements` — the artifact built to be the snapshot a
provider actually sees — rather than `payout_audits`, which records
*attempts* (RazorpayX's status frozen at creation, never updated when the
money lands) plus internal retries and nightly reconciliation repairs. A
provider reading those raw would see several rows for one payment.

Carries no admin id, gateway id or error text: a provider learns what
happened to their money, not who moved it or through which processor.

Lifetime earnings total for the signed-in provider (SVC-275).

A separate route rather than a fourth `range` value on the endpoint below,
because that one returns a row per booking: bounded over a window, unbounded
over a lifetime. Provider Home shows a single figure and should not pay for
every job the provider has ever done to render it.

Same definition of "earned" as the windowed endpoint (completed, not
refunded), shared via `ProviderService._earned_filter`. That is narrower than
the payout path's `_owed_filter`, which also excludes cash jobs: a cash job is
earned but not owed, since the provider already has the money.

The SP's earnings split by the Pro who did each job (SVC-323).

Same windows as `/me/earnings`, plus `all`. Every Pro of the SP is listed,
removed ones and those with no jobs included; jobs that completed with no
Pro on them are one `professional_id: null` "Not assigned" row. The totals
equal `/me/earnings` (windows) and `/me/earnings/summary` (`all`). Separate
from `GET /me/team`, which the pick-a-Pro step calls on every accept.

Provider earnings summary + per-booking breakdown for the chosen window.

Window is the IST calendar boundary (today = since 00:00 IST, week = since
Monday 00:00 IST, month = since the 1st 00:00 IST). Refunded payments are
excluded. Used by the provider Earnings dashboard (SC-27).

`professional_id` (SVC-323) narrows it to one of the SP's Pros, removed ones
included: the per-Pro detail view. Anyone else's Pro is a 404 `PRO_NOT_FOUND`.

post.description:
Cancel a booking on a customer's behalf (SVC-299).

Support-only escape hatch — bypasses the customer/provider valid-transition
rules so a stuck booking (partner ghosted en_route, wrong service dispatched,
obvious fraud) can be closed without opening a psql shell.

Refund inherits the consumer cancel policy in
``BookingService._apply_cancellation_policy`` (see there): a captured
online payment triggers a Razorpay refund minus the ``ACCEPTED`` / ``EN_ROUTE``
cancellation fee; PENDING and cash bookings are pure state changes with no
money movement. IN_PROGRESS is intentionally *not* auto-refunded — the
job has started, so support is expected to refund manually via the
payments surface after diagnosing.

``booking_status_logs`` gets a row with ``changed_by=admin.id`` and the
reason in the ``note`` column; ``booking.cancellation_reason`` is stamped
with the same string. Both parties get the standard cancelled push
(SVC-278, SVC-348) with the admin as actor so the notification tone matches
consumer-initiated cancels — the customer/provider hears "your booking
was cancelled", not the internal detail that support did it.

409.description: Booking is already in a terminal state

get.description:
Fetch any one booking by id, whoever it belongs to.

Distinct from ``GET /bookings/{id}``, which admits only that booking's own
consumer or assigned provider — an admin is neither, so the user-facing route
refuses them and there was previously no way for support to look at a single
booking at all.

This one carries the consumer's address, which the bulk listing above
deliberately does not (SVC-170). That is the whole distinction: one booking
asked for by id is a support question about a specific job, where a page of
every booking on the platform is a standing export of home addresses. It
still withholds the doorstep PIN — see ``BookingResponse.for_admin``.

Everything that happened to one booking, oldest first (SVC-333): status
changes (``type: "status"``) merged with changes of its Pro (``type:
"assignment"``: claimed, repicked, declined, released, provider_cancelled).

Answers "who was actually sent, by whom, and when" in a dispute. Its own
route rather than more fields on ``GET /admin/bookings/{id}``, which reuses
the consumer's ``BookingResponse``: Pro and actor names must never reach that
shape.

do we owe, and how much" for the admin payouts screen. Read-only, so it takes
the role guard rather than injecting the admin (nothing to audit).

Payout audit trail for a single provider, newest-first (SVC-300).

Paired with the pending-settlements list: the admin expands a row to see
what has already been paid before triggering a fresh payout, closing the

dispatch. Read-only projection over ``payout_audits`` — no state changes.

post.description:
Enqueue a RazorpayX payout for a provider's completed-but-unsettled bookings.

Returns 202 with a summary of what will be paid and the Celery task id. The
payout itself runs asynchronously (SVC-188 / G30): before this, the endpoint
awaited a 30-90s RazorpayX HTTP call while holding a DB connection and a
``SELECT … FOR UPDATE`` lock on the provider's pending bookings, which
puts pool pressure on the same workers serving consumer traffic during a
RazorpayX slowdown.

Before queuing, ``PayoutService.preflight_payout`` runs every check the task
would refuse on (KYC, payout details, nothing pending, an unresolved
attempt, wallet ≤ 0, the batch cap) with the same messages, read-only and
lock-free. A refusal is a 402 and nothing is queued. Before this only the cap
was checked here, and the rest came back as a 202 "queued" the task then
rolled back without a trace. The task runs the full flow (record audit → lock
rows → RazorpayX → resolve audit → update bookings → drain pushes) through
the same ``PayoutService.create_provider_payout``, which re-runs the checks
under the row lock and writes a ``refused`` audit row if one fails there.

Every attempt is still recorded in ``payout_audits`` before the RazorpayX
call fires; the admin payouts screen surfaces the outcome from there, and
``reconcile_payouts`` (nightly) resolves any breadcrumb whose task
process died mid-flight.

SVC-423: one ``admin_actions`` row per accepted request, committed before the
enqueue, because an unaudited money move is worse than a row for a failed
enqueue. A refused batch writes none, and the task writes none: each
attempt's outcome stays in ``payout_audits``. That's why the preflight runs
first: a 402/404 raises before the row is written.

Reset a provider's FAILED settlements to PENDING so they can be paid again.

Manual recovery for payouts that failed (bad bank details, KYC hold, ...): once
the cause is fixed, an admin re-queues the failed settlements, which then become
eligible for the next payout run. The triggering admin is recorded in the audit
trail.

Reset a provider's REVERSED settlements to PENDING so they can be paid again.

A reversal means the payout reached the provider and was then clawed back —
often a KYC/compliance signal, not a simple retry. Only use this once you've
confirmed the provider is genuinely still owed and the underlying cause is
fixed; otherwise the re-payment will likely bounce again. Admin-only and
recorded in the audit trail.

get.description:
One row per SP with any payout-scope booking (completed, PAID, not cash).

Count + paise per settlement status, ``earned_paise`` across all five, and
``payable_paise``, the net a payout would send now. ``status`` keeps SPs with a
booking in that bucket; omit it for all. Largest pending amount first.

The bookings behind an SP's payout figures, newest completion first, with the
price, commission and payout split each one contributed.

Payout-scope bookings completed on IST days ``from``..``to`` inclusive, as CSV
for the accounting import. At most 366 days. Cash bookings are left out.

post.description:
One-shot publish: bump `app_versions.{platform}` + (optionally) push
a "New version available" notification to every consumer with an
FCM token.

The two-step manual ritual — SQL update + separate broadcast call —
is easy to get wrong (bump the version without notifying, or notify
without bumping and users tap through to nothing new). This endpoint
does both atomically: the DB write happens first (so the poll-on-
foreground path immediately reflects the new version even if the
broadcast fails to enqueue), then the Celery task is fired.

Not the same as ``release-apk.yml`` — that builds and uploads the
APK. This endpoint tells the running fleet about it after the APK
is in place. The current publish ritual is:
  1. `gh workflow run release-apk.yml -f version=X.Y.Z`
  2. `POST /admin/app-versions/android/release {"version": "X.Y.Z"}`

get.description:
Liveness probe — the process is running.

Never touches the DB / Redis. Used by container orchestrators to decide
when to restart; a failed DB should NOT trigger a restart (that just
thrashes the pod without fixing anything).

Readiness probe — the process can actually serve requests.

Pings each dependency with a short timeout, returns a per-dependency
result. If ANY dependency fails, response is HTTP 503 (Service
Unavailable) — so load balancers can drain traffic from this pod without
also killing it.

AdminBookingVolume.title: AdminBookingVolume
AdminBookingVolume.description:
Bookings CREATED for this SP in the last 30 IST days, today included
(not completed ones): ``created_at`` on or after IST midnight of ``since``.
The same rule as ``GET /admin/bookings?provider_id=…&created_from=since``,
so that link lists exactly these rows. ``by_status`` has every status.

AdminCatalogCategoryNode.title: AdminCatalogCategoryNode
AdminCatalogCategoryNode.description:
A category in the tree. An L1 (``parent_id`` null) lists its
sub-categories in ``children``; a category holding services directly (an L2,
or an L1 like Miscellaneous) lists them in ``services``. Inactive rows are
included.

AdminCatalogServiceRow.title: AdminCatalogServiceRow
AdminCatalogServiceRow.description:
A service in the tree. ``active_variant_count`` counts the variants a
customer can pick; at 0 the service books at ``base_price``.
``active_bookings`` counts bookings that are requested, accepted, en route or
in progress.

AdminCatalogTree.title: AdminCatalogTree
AdminCatalogTree.description:
Every category and service, active or not. Categories are ordered by
``sort_order`` then name among their siblings; services by name.

AdminCategoryCreate.title: AdminCategoryCreate
AdminCategoryCreate.description:
A new category. The slug is made from the name and never changes.
``parent_id`` null makes an L1 (home tile); set, an L2 under that L1.

AdminCategoryDetail.title: AdminCategoryDetail
AdminCategoryDetail.description:
One category with what it holds. Deactivate is refused while
``active_service_count`` or ``active_subcategory_count`` is above 0.

AdminCategoryUpdate.title: AdminCategoryUpdate
AdminCategoryUpdate.description:
Any subset. ``parent_id: null`` makes it an L1 and ``icon_key: null``
clears the icon; ``null`` is refused for ``name`` and ``sort_order``.

AdminCouponCreate.title: AdminCouponCreate
AdminCouponCreate.description:
A new global coupon. ``code`` is trimmed and uppercased, then must match
``^[A-Z0-9]{3,20}$``. ``valid_from`` defaults to now. A datetime with no
offset is read as UTC.

AdminCouponDetail.title: AdminCouponDetail
AdminCouponDetail.description:
The row plus its usage: the total discount given and the latest 20
redemptions, newest first.

AdminCouponRow.title: AdminCouponRow
AdminCouponRow.description:
One coupon. ``user_id`` set = a personal (referral) coupon, owned by
``owner_name`` / ``owner_phone``. ``usage_count`` counts redemption rows, a
cancelled booking's included, which is the count the limits use.

AdminCouponUpdate.title: AdminCouponUpdate
AdminCouponUpdate.description:
Any subset of the editable fields. ``code``, ``user_id`` and ``is_active``
aren't editable here (deactivate / activate change the last). ``null`` clears
``max_discount``, ``min_order_amount`` or ``usage_limit`` and is refused on
the others.

AdminInviteRow.title: AdminInviteRow
AdminInviteRow.description:
An invite in the owner's history. No ``token``: a pending code is a live
credential, and support doesn't need it (the SP sees it in My Team).

AdminProDetail.title: AdminProDetail
AdminProDetail.description:
``GET /admin/pros/{id}``: the Pro, their owner, and (SVC-427) their
rating and completed jobs, by the SVC-396 trust-card rules: reviews and
COMPLETED bookings carrying this ``professional_id``.

AdminProListRow.title: AdminProListRow
AdminProListRow.description: ``GET /admin/pros`` (SVC-427): a Pro row and the owner it belongs to.

AdminProviderDetail.title: AdminProviderDetail
AdminProviderDetail.description:
``GET /admin/providers/{id}`` (SVC-427): the search row plus the SP
page's aggregates. A superset of the row, so older callers are unaffected.

AdminProviderRow.title: AdminProviderRow
AdminProviderRow.description: ``GET /admin/providers``: one owner (a user with a provider profile).

AdminProviderService.title: AdminProviderService
AdminProviderService.description:
A catalog service the SP offers. ``is_active`` is the catalog row's, so
a retired service can be shown as such.

AdminRole.title: AdminRole
AdminRole.description: What a ``role=ADMIN`` user may do in the console (SVC-422).

AdminServiceArea.title: AdminServiceArea
AdminServiceArea.description:
The SP's service area: a circle, since that's what is stored (a centre
point and a radius), not a polygon.

AdminServiceCreate.title: AdminServiceCreate
AdminServiceCreate.description:
A new service. ``min_qty`` is required for PER_SQFT / PER_HOUR and must be
left out (or null) for PER_VISIT / PER_ITEM. ``description`` is markdown,
stored as sent.

AdminServiceDeactivate.title: AdminServiceDeactivate
AdminServiceDeactivate.description:
``confirm: true`` deactivates even while bookings are in flight. They
carry on; only new bookings are refused.

AdminServiceDetail.title: AdminServiceDetail
AdminServiceDetail.description: The tree row plus the description and every variant, active or not.

AdminServiceUpdate.title: AdminServiceUpdate

and is refused on the others. Moving off PER_SQFT / PER_HOUR needs

AdminServiceVariantRow.title: AdminServiceVariantRow
AdminServiceVariantRow.description: Read-only here: variants are edited elsewhere.

AdminTeamPro.title: AdminTeamPro
AdminTeamPro.description: A Pro row as admin sees it: removed rows included (``is_active``).

AssignmentTimelineItem.title: AssignmentTimelineItem
AssignmentTimelineItem.description: A ``booking_assignment_events`` row: the booking's Pro changed.

BookingAddress.title: BookingAddress
BookingAddress.description:
Where the job is, as the booking's two parties see it (SVC-170).

Its own schema rather than a reuse of ``AddressResponse``, which backs the
consumer's own address book: that one carries ``is_default``, a detail of how
the consumer manages their saved addresses and nothing a provider standing
outside the building has any use for. Same principle that gave
``BookingOfferResponse`` its own shape (SVC-153) — serve each audience the
fields its screen actually renders.

``lat``/``lng`` are the point of this being a nested object rather than a bare
``full_address`` string. The job to be done is *navigate there*: with
coordinates the app can hand off to the device maps app, without them the
provider retypes a free-text Indian address into Google Maps and trusts its
geocoder — the failure mode this ticket exists to remove. ``get_offer``
already reads the same geography to derive ``distance_km``.

Both are optional because ``location`` is nullable: ``CreateAddressRequest``
accepts an address with no coordinates, and older rows have none. Clients must
treat text as the source of truth and coordinates as the enhancement, never
the reverse.

BookingItemResponse.title: BookingItemResponse
BookingItemResponse.description:
One line on a booking response.

``service_name`` is denormalised into the response so the mobile app
doesn't have to cross-reference against /services for every booking it
displays — the list route already returns dozens of items and doing that
lookup client-side is exactly the sort of N+1 pattern the frontend keeps
hitting. Read from the loaded ``BookingItem.service`` relationship, which
must be eager-loaded (see ``BookingItem.service`` — ``raise_on_sql``).

BookingOfferResponse.title: BookingOfferResponse
BookingOfferResponse.description:
What a broadcast recipient may see about a job they have not yet accepted.

Deliberately its own schema rather than a reuse of ``BookingResponse`` (SVC-153).
This is served to *every* nearby provider, none of whom is assigned yet, so it
carries only what the Incoming Request Card renders — and notably not
``doorstep_otp``, which gates the en_route → in_progress transition and must
reach the provider from the consumer at the door, not from this API.

``service_amount`` is returned as a plain number; the app formats the ₹ string.
Rupee formatting is not done server-side here — see the ticket's money note.

``expires_at`` and ``seconds_remaining`` both describe the same instant and are
both returned on purpose (SVC-166). The card's countdown must use
``seconds_remaining``: it is computed server-side, so a device with a wrong
clock still counts down correctly, and clock skew is unbounded on a 120-second
window. ``expires_at`` is the absolute form, for anything needing a real
instant rather than a duration.

Neither field carries a default — a defaulted field falls out of OpenAPI
``required`` and the generated client types it optional, which invites a
``?? 120`` fallback and reintroduces the bug this exists to fix.

BookingStatusLogResponse.title: BookingStatusLogResponse
BookingStatusLogResponse.description:
One state transition on a booking, as the tracking timeline sees it.

A deliberately narrow projection of ``booking_status_logs``, which is an
internal audit trail and not a consumer-facing record (SVC-248). Two
columns are withheld on purpose:

``changed_by`` is a user id — usually the assigned provider's, sometimes an
admin's. Who moved a booking is an operational fact; handing it to the
consumer's app turns an audit row into a disclosure about another person.

``metadata_`` is free-form JSONB written by whatever called
``_log_transition``. Nobody has audited what is already in those rows
across the project's history, and a field whose contents are unknown
cannot be knowingly published. If some part of it is worth showing, it
should be promoted to a named column first.

``from_status`` is left out for a plainer reason: on an ordered list the
previous state is always the ``to_status`` of the entry before it.

CategoryPricingRow.title: CategoryPricingRow
CategoryPricingRow.description: One category with its pricing config. L1 rows have no parent.

CategoryPricingUpdate.title: CategoryPricingUpdate
CategoryPricingUpdate.description:
Any subset of the six fields. ``null`` clears ``reference_price`` or
``bounds_pct`` and is refused on the others. Turning ``is_sensitive`` on
needs ``bounds_pct`` in the same body unless the row already has bounds.

CouponResponse.title: CouponResponse
CouponResponse.description:
One coupon in a user's available list.

``discount_type`` lets the UI render the correct microcopy
("20% off" vs "₹100 off") without needing to know the value's units
from context. ``expires_at`` is what the card renders — the internal
``valid_from`` is not exposed, a coupon that hasn't started yet simply
doesn't appear in the list.

CouponValidateRequest.title: CouponValidateRequest
CouponValidateRequest.description: User taps [Apply] on a coupon; the app asks the backend to price it.

CreateBookingItemRequest.title: CreateBookingItemRequest
CreateBookingItemRequest.description: One line item on a booking-creation request.

CreateBookingRequest.title: CreateBookingRequest
CreateBookingRequest.description:
Create a booking as either a multi-item cart (``items``) or a single
service (``service_id``).

``service_id`` is the legacy single-service shape retained for the mobile
app while the cart UI is rolling out (PR 2c). It is normalised to a
1-item ``items`` list inside the validator so the service layer sees one
shape. Once the cart UI has shipped everywhere the ``service_id`` field
can be removed and callers forced onto ``items``.

DeleteAccountRequest.title: DeleteAccountRequest
DeleteAccountRequest.description:
Optional body for ``DELETE /users/me`` (SVC-367).

The refresh token, when sent, is revoked like ``/auth/logout`` does. It is
optional because the account going inactive already makes every refresh
token for it fail; this just puts the caller's on the blacklist too.

DiscountType.title: DiscountType
DiscountType.description:
How ``Coupon.discount_value`` reduces the bill.

``PERCENT``: value is a percent (0–100). ``max_discount`` caps the
resulting rupee amount — a "20% off" without a cap on a big cart would
give away the whole store.

``FLAT``: value is a rupee amount. Capped at the cart total at
application time (see the coupon service) so a ₹500-off coupon on a
₹200 cart discounts ₹200, not ₹500.

EarningsByProResponse.title: EarningsByProResponse
EarningsByProResponse.description:
The SP's earnings split by Pro (SVC-323). ``total_payout`` and
``completed_count`` equal ``/me/earnings`` for a window and
``/me/earnings/summary`` for ``all``.

EarningsProfessional.title: EarningsProfessional
EarningsProfessional.description: The Pro who did an earnings row's job (SVC-323).

EarningsSummaryResponse.title: EarningsSummaryResponse
EarningsSummaryResponse.description:
All-time totals, with no per-booking breakdown (SVC-275).

Deliberately two scalars. ``EarningsResponse`` carries one row per booking,
which is fine over a window and unbounded over a lifetime — Provider Home
would download every job a provider has ever completed to render a single
number.

ForceCancelBookingRequest.title: ForceCancelBookingRequest
ForceCancelBookingRequest.description:
Admin-driven cancel request (SVC-299).

Same shape as ``KYCRejectionRequest`` — one required free-text reason,
500-char ceiling. ``min_length=1`` rather than the 5 the consumer cancel
schema imposes: support can legitimately write "duplicate" or "fraud"
and reserving stricter validation to the consumer path keeps that gate
where it exists to slow accidental one-tap cancels, not admin ones.

KYCDocsResponse.title: KYCDocsResponse
KYCDocsResponse.description: Admin-only: full KYC payload including presigned doc URLs for review.

KYCQueueCountResponse.title: KYCQueueCountResponse
KYCQueueCountResponse.description: How many rows the admin KYC queue has across all pages (SVC-424).

KYCQueueRow.title: KYCQueueRow
KYCQueueRow.description:
One row in the admin KYC queue listing (SVC-298).

Shape is a UserResponse plus the three ProviderProfile timestamps the review
UI wants for aging + the rejected view. Kept separate from UserResponse
because those are provider-only columns — surfacing them on every user list
would be schema noise.

LatestVersionResponse.title: LatestVersionResponse
LatestVersionResponse.description:
The whole payload returned by GET /downloads/latest.json.

Shape is stable — the frontend hook branches on the presence of each
platform key. Adding a new platform means adding a new required key
here + a matching row in ``app_versions``, as ``ios`` did (SVC-366).

LogoutRequest.title: LogoutRequest
LogoutRequest.description:
SVC-241: refresh token to blacklist. The access token is short-lived
and expires on its own; the refresh token is the durable credential a
thief could otherwise use to mint fresh access tokens for 30 days.

NearbyProviderResponse.title: NearbyProviderResponse
NearbyProviderResponse.description: Slim response for the 'nearby providers' discovery endpoint.

PayoutBookingRow.title: PayoutBookingRow
PayoutBookingRow.description: One booking behind an SP's payout figures: the split that went into it.

PayoutDashboardProvider.title: PayoutDashboardProvider
PayoutDashboardProvider.description: One SP with any payout-scope booking (completed, PAID, not cash).

PayoutMethod.title: PayoutMethod
PayoutMethod.description:
Which stored destination a provider's payouts actually go to.

A provider may keep both a UPI handle and a bank account on file (SVC-148:
switching does not erase the old one). This is the single source of truth for
which one the money is sent to — the payout must never infer it from which
columns happen to be populated.

PayoutMethodSelect.title: PayoutMethodSelect
PayoutMethodSelect.description: Switch payouts to a method the provider already has stored (SVC-148).

PendingSettlementProvider.title: PendingSettlementProvider
PendingSettlementProvider.description: One provider with money owed, as shown in the admin payouts list.

PendingSettlementsResponse.title: PendingSettlementsResponse
PendingSettlementsResponse.description:
Capped list of providers awaiting settlement.

Not paginated by design (SVC-144): the admin panel shows one screen of who is
owed. ``total`` is the true number of providers with pending settlements, so the
UI can say "showing 200 of 247" when ``truncated`` is set.

PlatformVersion.title: PlatformVersion
PlatformVersion.description:
Version metadata for one platform (android / pwa / ios).

``version`` and ``min_supported_version`` are SemVer strings. Clients
compare using SemVer semantics — a lex compare would treat 1.10 < 1.2.

ProEarningsItem.title: ProEarningsItem
ProEarningsItem.description:
One Pro's share of the SP's earnings in a range (SVC-323).

``professional_id`` None is the "Not assigned" row: jobs that completed with
no Pro on them, so the rows always add up to the SP's total. That row has
``is_self`` and ``is_active`` False and no photo.

ProKYCDocsResponse.title: ProKYCDocsResponse
ProKYCDocsResponse.description:
Admin-only: a team Pro's KYC review payload (SVC-327) — the SP payload
plus which Pro row it is and which SP they work for.

ProMeResponse.title: ProMeResponse
ProMeResponse.description:
``GET /pros/me``. ``kyc_status`` is the KYC that applies to this person:
their own Aadhaar KYC, or for a Pro-for-self, the SP's.

ProfessionalBrief.title: ProfessionalBrief
ProfessionalBrief.description:
Who is doing the job (SVC-324): the assigned Pro, as a booking shows them.

No phone here: the consumer gets the Pro's number only through
``BookingResponse.provider_phone`` (SVC-360, interim until masked calling),
which is gated by viewer and status, and the SP doesn't need it from here.
``is_self`` marks the SP's own Pro-for-self, so a client can collapse
"Rohan from Rohan" to one name on a solo job.

The trust fields (SVC-396) are this Pro's own record, not the SP's: reviews
and completed bookings whose ``professional_id`` is this Pro. They are set
by ``BookingService.attach_professionals`` in one grouped query per page,
and defaulted so the brief stays additive. ``rating_average`` is null until
the first review. ``is_background_verified`` is the Pro's effective KYC
(a Pro-for-self's is its SP's), verified or not.

ProfessionalResponse.title: ProfessionalResponse
ProfessionalResponse.description: A Pro row. ``is_self`` marks an SP's Pro-for-self.

ProviderPayoutEntry.title: ProviderPayoutEntry
ProviderPayoutEntry.description:
One settlement cycle, as the provider sees it.

Deliberately carries no ``payout_audit_id``, RazorpayX id, admin or error.
A provider learns what happened to their money, never who moved it or
through which processor.

ProviderPayoutHistoryEntry.title: ProviderPayoutHistoryEntry
ProviderPayoutHistoryEntry.description:
One row from the payout audit trail for a single provider (SVC-300).

Mirrors the ``payout_audits`` row directly rather than inventing new field
names — the admin history view is the ledger, and drift between the two
invites "the row I see is not the row that moved" bugs.

ProviderPayoutHistoryResponse.title: ProviderPayoutHistoryResponse
ProviderPayoutHistoryResponse.description: Paginated payout history for one provider, newest-first.

ProviderPayoutSummaryResponse.title: ProviderPayoutSummaryResponse
ProviderPayoutSummaryResponse.description:
What the next transfer will actually send, and what the last one did.

Three money figures rather than one, because they genuinely differ and the
difference is the thing this ticket exists to explain:

* ``pending_amount`` is ``min(wallet_balance, booking_sum)`` — what the
  payout will really send.
* ``gross_amount`` is what those jobs are worth before netting.
* ``balance_owed`` is set only when the provider owes the platform more than
  it owes them, which happens after a run of cash work.

A provider told "₹3,480 coming" who receives ₹2,900 has been misled by their
own app, so the headline figure is the net one and the gap is named.

ProviderProfileUpdate.title: ProviderProfileUpdate
ProviderProfileUpdate.description: Fields a provider can update on their own profile.

url.title: Url
url.description: New APK URL. Usually stays the same because release-apk.yml overwrites apk/latest.apk in place.

notify.title: Notify
notify.description: Fire the FCM broadcast so users learn about the update without opening the app.

PublishReleaseRequest.title: PublishReleaseRequest
PublishReleaseRequest.description:
Bump the current version + optionally push a nudge to every device.

``version`` is the customer-facing SemVer of the new build. The
matching APK must already be at ``app_versions.url`` (usually
``s3://eazyserv-downloads/apk/latest.apk``, since ``release-apk.yml``
always overwrites that key). If they don't match, users will nudge
themselves onto a version we haven't shipped yet.

``min_supported_version``, when passed, atomically hard-blocks anyone
below it — the SVC-162 emergency lever. Leave it unset to keep the
current threshold.

``notify`` = true enqueues the FCM broadcast (``broadcast_update_available``).
Set to false when releasing a build we don't want to interrupt users
over (e.g. a silent metrics fix — the poll on next foreground will
still surface the nudge).

task_id.title: Task Id
task_id.description: Celery task id for the FCM broadcast (only when notify=true).

PushCapabilityReport.title: PushCapabilityReport
PushCapabilityReport.description:
What the client can tell us about its ability to receive push (SVC-255).

Sent on every registration attempt, successful or not. That "or not" is the
whole point: Sentry already records failures, but with no denominator —
"12 failures this week" is unreadable without knowing whether that is 12 out
of 12 or 12 out of 400. Reporting every attempt supplies the denominator.

Nothing here is stored. The handler logs one line and returns; the question
it answers ("how many providers can actually receive push, and on what?") is
a one-off scoping question, not a per-user fact worth a column.

RelatedServiceEntry.title: RelatedServiceEntry
RelatedServiceEntry.description:
One entry in a related-services rail on the service detail page (SVC-292).

Denormalises name + base_price so the frontend renders the three rails
in the same round trip that fetches the service itself — no per-row
lookups from the client. ``sort_order`` is preserved so the frontend
respects the seed's / admin's ordering.

RelatedServicesBucket.title: RelatedServicesBucket
RelatedServicesBucket.description:
The three related-services surfaces the redesigned service page renders.

Names track the three ``relationship_type`` enum values so the mapping
from row to render surface is 1:1 — no server-side re-shaping. An empty
list is a legitimate answer (a service with no seeded hooks, for example)
and the frontend renders nothing for that surface.

ReviewSnippet.title: ReviewSnippet
ReviewSnippet.description:
SVC-388: one customer quote for a service card.

``created_at`` rather than "N days ago" so a cached response never goes
stale; the frontend formats it. ``reviewer_first_name`` is None for a
deleted or nameless reviewer, and the frontend shows its fallback label.

ServiceDetailResponse.title: ServiceDetailResponse
ServiceDetailResponse.description:
``GET /services/{id}`` response — the ServiceResponse shape plus the
three related-services buckets from SVC-291.

Kept as a subclass so the plain-list ``GET /services`` endpoint stays
lean (no related payload per row across dozens of catalogue entries)
and the per-service fetch pays exactly one extra roundtrip's worth of
joins to surface the rails.

ServiceProviderBrief.title: ServiceProviderBrief
ServiceProviderBrief.description: The business behind the job (SVC-324): the SP's brand, never payout details.

ServiceStep.title: ServiceStep
ServiceStep.description:
SVC-400: the richer step shape. ``icon`` is a free-form keyword the
frontend maps to a Lucide icon.

ServiceVariantResponse.title: ServiceVariantResponse
ServiceVariantResponse.description:
One priced option under a service.

``base_price`` is what the customer sees before GST; ``gst_percent`` is 0
for the launch summary rows and 18 for the vertical sheets. Frontend
computes the customer total as ``base_price * (1 + gst_percent/100)``
when rendering the checkout.

``provider_payout`` + ``platform_commission`` are stored, not derived,
because the split ratio isn't a global constant — the launch summary
rows are 70/30 and the vertical sheets are 65/35. The booking service
snapshots these fields into ``booking_items`` at booking time.

SettlementStatus.title: SettlementStatus
SettlementStatus.description:
Provider-payout lifecycle. Driven by ``PayoutService`` — every read/write of
``bookings.settlement_status`` goes through it.

StatusTimelineItem.title: StatusTimelineItem
StatusTimelineItem.description:
A ``booking_status_logs`` row. ``metadata`` is withheld for the reason
``BookingStatusLogResponse`` gives: free-form JSONB nobody has audited.

TeamInviteResponse.title: TeamInviteResponse
TeamInviteResponse.description:
The SP's view of one invite.

Carries the code (``token``) and the static ``/invite`` URL. The SP is the
one sending it, so they can pass the code on another way if the SMS doesn't
arrive; it only works from the invited phone.

TeamPickPro.title: TeamPickPro
TeamPickPro.description: One row of the pick-a-Pro modal.

TeamPickResponse.title: TeamPickResponse
TeamPickResponse.description:
202 from ``PATCH /bookings/{id}/accept`` with ``X-Team-Pick: 1``, for a
team SP. Nothing has been claimed: the claim is ``POST /bookings/{id}/assign``.

TimelinePro.title: TimelinePro
TimelinePro.description: A Pro as the admin timeline names them.

TipBookingRequest.title: TipBookingRequest
TipBookingRequest.description:
Consumer adds (or updates) a gratuity on a completed booking.

Zero is a valid amount — the client uses this to *remove* a tip the
consumer changed their mind about before payout has flowed. Bounded
at ₹10,000 so a fat-finger doesn't move real money by accident;
higher values need to route through support.

UpdateAddressRequest.title: UpdateAddressRequest
UpdateAddressRequest.description:
Edit a saved address (SVC-277). Every field optional — this is a PATCH.

Served by a copy-on-write update: the old row is soft-deleted and a new one
created, so bookings that already point at the old address keep recording
where the job actually happened. See `UserService.update_address`.

UpdateFCMTokenRequest.title: UpdateFCMTokenRequest
UpdateFCMTokenRequest.description:
Register or clear the caller's FCM token.

`fcm_token` is nullable but *required* — `null` clears the stored token
(sign-out), while an omitted field is a 422. Without that distinction an
empty body would silently wipe push for the user.

`platform` (SVC-371) says which app the token belongs to, so the release
push can skip other platforms. It is optional, unlike the ticket's wording:
installed APKs predate it and a required field would 422 their
registration, losing them push entirely. Omitted means stored as NULL,
which still gets every release push.

UpdateLanguageRequest.title: UpdateLanguageRequest
UpdateLanguageRequest.description:
Body for ``PATCH /users/me/language`` (SVC-374).

Required and never null: there is no way back to "never chosen", which
would re-show the app's one-time prompt. Anything but the three codes is
a 422.
